articles.title: Action Jets: Learning the Local Shape of the Action-conditioned Data Manifold
articles.excerpt: World models are a powerful means of reasoning and planning, but many of these action-conditioned predictive models are high dimensional and computationally expensive. These challenges limit the number of action candidates that can be evaluated by a planner. We show that this cost is avoidable for planners over short horizons, which only require local information with respect to the current state. For a fixed state, the frames reachable by varying a low-dimensional action (a camera movement or an end-effector command) lie on a low-dimensional manifold. We estimate the local shape of that manifold directly via a network trained to estimate how each image region moves per unit of each action axis supervised by data collected from samples by the generator. A correction head fit to trajectory data estimates the shape of this manifold region up to a third-order Taylor polynomial. We call this network estimating the Taylor polynomial describing the manifold shape an Action Jet and compute its radius of validity in closed form. By traversing this approximation of the local manifold shape, we only have to perform inference once per state for any number of candidate actions. Scoring sixteen candidates from a single extraction is over 300x faster than with either source generator, and this gap widens with the number of candidates a planner evaluates. We measure against state-of-the-art action-conditioned generators, IRASim and WorldGym on BridgeData V2, a real 7-DoF manipulation benchmark, and FrameCrafter on DL3DV scenes, where we chart from the novel-view generators DepthSplat and LagerNVS. Because only the tangent comes from the generator and every other term from the data, the Action Jet also predicts held-out frames more accurately than IRASim, the generator that supplied its tangent, at short horizons and at over 100x less compute.

articles.title: How Far Can Coding Agents Go in Visual Generation?
articles.excerpt: Modern image generation largely relies on specialized generative models that leave the process of image construction implicit in learned parameters. We explore an alternative: general-purpose coding agents that construct images through executable programs. Our study of zero-shot drawing on AgentDrawBench, a 200-prompt benchmark, reveals a distinctive capability profile. Agents excel at preserving structure and satisfying precise visual constraints, achieving competitive results in domains where compositional accuracy matters more than photorealistic appearance, while remaining limited in perceptual richness. Their visual expressiveness varies with the drawing interface, and a qualitative study on reconstruction shows how procedural skills extracted from human demonstrations support different artistic media. We then examine code as an external visual language of thought: a structured, executable representation that agents can construct and inspect. We test it in visual question answering task and find reconstructed visual code retains substantial information for question answering and, in some domains, supports higher accuracy than the original image. These abilities raise a further question: do agents draw on a shared internal representation of scene content beyond a particular drawing program? We explore an internal visual language-of-thought hypothesis, in which a shared, compositionally structured representation supports visual operations across drawing languages. Cross-harness drawings and images assembled from independent single-pixel queries exhibit related layouts and tones. Agents also maintain self-generated room arrangements across viewpoints after visible drawings are removed. These results demonstrate that the coding agent would maintain a consistent and coherent world inside its imagine even before the harness gets involved and the generation starts.

articles.title: Why Do VLMs Fail at Remote Physiological Measurement? Rethinking with Physiological Grounding and Numerical Alignment
articles.excerpt: Video-based remote physiological measurement (RPM) has broad applications, while Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide a promising opportunity to enable end-to-end physiological monitoring for future human-aware intelligent systems. However, existing RPM methods rely on task-specific models and cannot be seamlessly integrated with the multimodal understanding and interaction capabilities of VLMs. We revisit RPM with VLMs and provide empirical evidence for two major bottlenecks: generic visual semantic representations fail to preserve fine-grained physiological cues; while discrete token prediction in autoregressive generation is inherently misaligned with continuous numerical measurement. To address these challenges, we propose VITAL (Visual-physiological Token Alignment for Language Models), a visual-physiological token alignment framework for RPM and preserving general vision tasks. VITAL retains the original visual pathway for semantic understanding and introduces an independent physiological pathway to jointly model semantic and physiological information. Moreover, we propose a structured numerical alignment approach to improve the reliability of generative heart rate estimation by enhancing numerical relationship modeling. Extensive experiments show that VITAL improves cross-domain estimation performance on multiple rPPG datasets while preserving the general visual understanding capability of VLMs, demonstrating its effectiveness as a unified visual-physiological model. Code will be released.

articles.title: WorldMemBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Memory of Video World Models
articles.excerpt: As video models enable longer and more realistic interactive experiences, maintaining a world consistent with its history becomes essential. This requires both preserving previously observed content and ensuring coherent world evolution over time. World memory is a critical capability to evaluate alongside visual fidelity and video duration. We introduce WorldMemBench, a benchmark for systematically evaluating world memory in video world models. Across 260 test cases, it assesses static memory through the retention of human identity and appearance, object appearance and geometry, and environmental content and geometry, and dynamic memory through event progression and state persistence. Using controlled camera departures and multi-revisit trajectories, the benchmark evaluates static content against fixed initial references and dynamic events against expected state transitions. It combines appearance and geometry metrics with event-specific assessments, and reports video quality and camera-following accuracy as complementary diagnostics. Evaluation of nine representative models shows that strong static retention does not imply reliable dynamic state evolution, while repeated revisits reveal memory degradation beyond the first return. Human studies support the alignment between our automatic evaluations and human judgments. WorldMemBench provides a systematic testbed for diagnosing memory failures and guiding the development of persistent, temporally coherent video worlds.

articles.title: MonoMIP: Multi-Height Inverse Perspective Mapping for Monocular 3D Object Detection
articles.excerpt: Monocular 3D object detection methods increasingly rely on depth-guided transformers, but they operate entirely in the perspective image plane where spatial relationships are distorted by foreshortening. We propose MonoMIP, a dual-decoder framework that adds complementary 3D geometric reasoning through Bird's-Eye View (BEV) features constructed via Multi-Height Inverse Perspective Mapping. We perform IPM at K elevation planes spanning ground to rooftop, producing an ordered stack of height-conditioned metric BEV features that reduces above-ground misprojection and exposes depth-dependent appearance variation across planes. A BEV decoder with multi-scale deformable attention aggregates this multi-height evidence per query, while a depth-guided 3D decoder provides complementary perspective-space predictions. Without extra training data, MonoMIP attains 25.84% Moderate AP3D|R40 on KITTI val and 21.66% on the official test set for Car, outperforming recent published monocular methods on both the KITTI and Waymo benchmarks.

articles.title: The Gap Is in the Geometry: A Convergent Meta-Analysis of Multi-Facet Aerial and Remote Sensing Video Understanding
articles.excerpt: Aerial and remote sensing video is increasingly evaluated like web video, by posing multiple-choice questions to multimodal large language models (MLLMs) over sampled frames and reporting accuracy. This paper argues that this recipe measures the wrong aspect, and supports the claim with a convergent meta-analysis of a broad set of published results, organized in four evidence tiers, in which a claim becomes a position only when collected evidence agrees. Parameter scale exhibits a median of +3.4 accuracy points per tenfold increase on aerial benchmarks, far below a human gap of at least 19 points, whereas acquisition conditions control perception, as 315 of 318 evaluations in 19 within-paper contrasts lose accuracy when conditions such as altitude, view, object size or time horizon become harder. No aerial benchmark in the corpus combines video input with per-task human and random baselines, competence collapses from answering to acting in closed-loop navigation, and the same MLLMs score higher on the aerial benchmark than on ground spatial ones, but lower on studies that test cross-view geometry. From these findings the current study derives five falsifiable principles and proposes the AVU-Card, a reporting card for aerial video benchmarks

articles.title: Towards a Data-Centric Understanding of Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
articles.excerpt: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have been widely applied in embodied agents and robotics for vision tasks. However, MLLMs suffer from limitations in spatial reasoning and perception. Post-training techniques have shown promise for improving these capabilities; yet, there are limited data-driven surveys of such approaches. In this survey, we consider approaches to fine-tuning pretrained MLLMs for spatial reasoning tasks, ranging from supervised to reinforcement learning, with an emphasis on the datasets used. We investigate themes of dataset construction, data modality and annotation, and evaluation of the resulting models. Based on these themes, we categorize research into three groups: dataset design, dataset construction and evaluation. We find four main methods for constructing fixed spatial annotations: rules and templates, LLM prompting, procedural generation, and human-in-the-loop. We also observe substantial variation in evaluation approaches, including different scoring methods, tolerance metrics, and benchmark types. Finally, we identify opportunities for future research in unified dynamic annotation, efficient spatial reasoning, standardization of evaluation, expanded spatial range, and human-centered spatial interactions.
articles.content: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have been widely applied in embodied agents and robotics for vision tasks. Post-training techniques have shown promise for improving these capabilities; yet, there are limited data-driven surveys of such approaches. In this survey, we consider approaches to fine-tuning pretrained MLLMs for spatial reasoning tasks, ranging from supervised to reinforcement learning, with an emphasis on the datasets used. We investigate themes of dataset construction, data modality and annotation, and evaluation of the resulting models. Based on these themes, we categorize research into three groups: dataset design, dataset construction and evaluation. We find four main methods for constructing fixed spatial annotations: rules and templates, LLM prompting, procedural generation, and human-in-the-loop. We also observe substantial variation in evaluation approaches, including different scoring methods, tolerance metrics, and benchmark types. Finally, we identify opportunities for future research in unified dynamic annotation, efficient spatial reasoning, standardization of evaluation, expanded spatial range, and human-centered spatial interactions.

articles.title: Into the LidarVerse: A Real-Time Unified LiDAR World Model Across Tasks and Sensors
articles.excerpt: We present LidarVerse, a real-time unified LiDAR world model for sensor simulation across tasks and sensors. Existing LiDAR simulators largely follow one of two complementary paradigms: reconstruction-based methods preserve the geometry of a captured scene but require lengthy per-scene optimization, whereas generative methods amortize learning across data but lack the consistency needed for long-horizon rollouts. LidarVerse brings both paradigms into a single, unified conditional generative framework. A universal tokenizer maps LiDAR range sequences into a shared latent space, where a bidirectional teacher learns a common interface for conditioning on a LiDAR prefix, an HD-Map, a persistent spatial cache, and optionally, text. Varying the available scene evidence turns the same model into a generator of new worlds, a point-cloud forecaster, or a generalizable resimulator of observed scenes without per-scene optimization. We distill the teacher into a four-step autoregressive causal student and maintain both a rolling temporal K/V cache and a world-aligned spatial cache, enabling persistent long-horizon rollouts with real-time inference at 11 FPS on a single H100 GPU. LidarVerse achieves state-of-the-art performance on most reported metrics across all three evaluation protocols, while its tokenizer supports 32-, 64-, and 128-beam LiDAR and generalizes to an unseen scanning pattern. These results demonstrate that generative and reconstruction-grounded LiDAR simulation can be realized within one model, providing the core capabilities for future closed-loop sensor simulation.

articles.title: Decoupled Drift-Diffusion World Models for Consistent Future Frame Prediction
articles.excerpt: World models of visual information predict future image frames conditioned on given action sequences. This predicted scene evolution is driven by deterministic changes such as controlled motion on a robot platform, as well as stochastic changes such as rendering of manipulated objects or previously occluded regions. Our key insight is that the spatial location of these stochastic changes is itself learnable. We leverage this insight by jointly regressing both the deterministic next-state prediction and the spatial uncertainty map, then using the uncertainty map to guide a conditional diffusion process. We propose Decoupled Drift-Diffusion World Model (D3WM), which uses a transformer trained with a Gaussian negative-log-likelihood objective to produce both the deterministic next-state prediction and a spatial map of heteroscedastic aleatoric uncertainty. The learned uncertainty map then provides a structured spatial gate for a conditional diffusion model: deterministic regions are anchored to the predicted state, while uncertain regions, such as disocclusions or dynamic textures, are sampled by the diffusion process. We frame this decomposition under a variance-gated stochastic differential equation that separates deterministic drift from stochastic diffusion. D3WM shows improved results over competitive baselines in two distinct types of action spaces: robotic tabletop manipulation and camera motion.

articles.title: A Gradient-Regularized Deep Learning Method for Restoring Image in Myopic Vision
articles.excerpt: Myopic vision degrades the quality of human vision due to spherical eye defocus aberrations that impair the perception of fine spatial details. To address this limitation, this work proposes a deep learning-based approach to computationally design transformed images that allow individuals with myopia in fixed distance to perceive scenes with enhanced clarity. The method trains a neural network to counteract defocus aberrations modeled using the second-order Zernike polynomial $Z_2^0$. The approach employs a U-Net architecture trained with a loss function combining reconstruction error minimization with spatial difference structural preservation through $\ell_1$ regularization. Training is carried out exclusively on the KITTI dataset, while testing is performed on DIV2K and ImageNet datasets, demonstrating generalization across diverse image distributions. Under myopic conditions modeled by $Z_2^0$, baseline performance shows visual degradation with PSNR values ranging from 19.47 to 27.42 dB across datasets and severity levels. The proposed gradient-regularized method achieves consistent improvements, delivering PSNR gains ranging from 1.48 to 7.34 dB and significantly lower perceptual compared to classical baselines.

articles.title: Long-horizon Video Generation with Slot Memory Addressed By Region Tokens
articles.excerpt: Memory for long-horizon video generation must satisfy two competing requirements: it must remain bounded so generation can continue indefinitely, while still recovering what was observed at a place when the camera returns, regardless of how long ago it was seen. Reconstruction-based memories provide spatial recall by caching and reprojecting explicit geometry, but require growing storage and depend on estimated 3D structure. Recurrent memories keep a constant-size state, but retention is governed by temporal recurrence, causing old observations to fade with time. We introduce SMART, a slot memory addressed by region tokens, which combines bounded storage with spatially addressed recall. SMART stores content in a constant-size slot recurrence whose writes are addressed by the observing camera and whose reads are queried by the rendering camera, without constructing an explicit 3D representation or maintaining a growing cache. Consequently, recall is conditioned on inter-view geometry rather than on recency. Each read additionally provides a confidence estimate that conditions a chunk-causal diffusion transformer, allowing it to selectively trust retrieved content while relying on its generative prior elsewhere. On long trajectories in Memory Maze and Minecraft, SMART maintains high-fidelity recall far beyond its training horizon while using constant memory and per-step cost.

articles.title: Kandinsky S2V 1.0: Audio-Driven Avatar Video Generation
articles.excerpt: We present Kandinsky S2V 1.0, an open family of speech-to-video models for controllable audio-driven human animation, comprising Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite (2B parameters) and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro (21B parameters). From a single reference image, a speech waveform, and a text prompt, the models generate long-form 25 FPS video in which lip motion, expression, pose, and gesture follow the speech. The architecture draws text and audio conditioning from one Qwen2.5-Omni model and adds a reference-aware three-scale visual memory. Training starts from the Kandinsky 5.0 Video foundation models [1] and combines mixed reference-memory layouts with an area-adaptive face loss. The training corpus contains 1.17M single-speaker clips selected by active-speaker detection, with captions generated directly in English and Russian. A side-by-side human evaluation against the strongest open-source baseline and two proprietary commercial models shows that Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro performs comparably to or better than these models on average and is also preferred for lip synchronization. On common speech to video benchmarks, Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro rank among the top performing models according to mean rank over five reported metrics. Beyond the base models, we provide {\pi}-Flow distilled variants of both Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro. The distilled Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro model generates video in 16 sampling steps without classifier-free guidance, achieving a 5.4 times end-to-end speedup over the base model, while matching or exceeding it on nearly all reported benchmark metrics. To accelerate open research and deployment in speech-to-video generation, we release the code, model checkpoints, and diffusers integration under the MIT license.

articles.title: SonoWorld: Towards Interactive Pose-Controllable Ultrasound World Models
articles.excerpt: Robotic ultrasound can standardize image acquisition and reduce operator workload and variability, but policy learning remains limited by the lack of realistic, controllable simulation environments. While controllable world models have advanced rapidly in natural-image domains, ultrasound world modeling remains challenging because each frame captures only a cross-section of unobserved 3D anatomy, causing small probe motions to induce large appearance changes. Existing approaches rely on robot-tracked poses and latent-space prediction, but do not directly generate the observations required for interactive control. We propose SonoWorld, a causal ultrasound world model that learns video dynamics from unlabeled clinical videos and grounds them to 6-DoF control using a small set of freehand clinical scans tracked with an EM sensor. SonoWorld is trained in three stages: pretraining a latent-action-conditioned video diffusion model on around 6.9 million unlabeled multi-organ ultrasound frames; grounding the learned video dynamics to metric probe poses with a small EM-tracked thyroid dataset; and applying distribution matching distillation to enable causal, long-horizon autoregressive generation with selectively caching eviction tokens at inference time. We evaluate controllability through pose-following fidelity, round-trip consistency, and axis-specific control under synthetic actions on held-out tracked scans, and further validate it with a user study. In model-based action discrimination, SonoWorld correctly ranks the target-directed probe motion over an equal-magnitude opposite motion in up to 74.8% of trials. To our knowledge, SonoWorld is the first causal, pose-controllable ultrasound world model learned primarily from freehand clinical videos, providing a data-driven interactive environment for robotic ultrasound data acquisition and policy evaluation.

articles.title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness
articles.excerpt: LLM system capabilities depend not only on model parameters but also on the executable harnesses that organize information acquisition, tool use, reasoning, and memory. Recursive harness evolution can automate their design, but how it can reliably discover generalizable systems from limited, noisy, and repeatedly reused feedback remains unclear. We study this question in agentic video understanding, where rich multimodal evidence and coupled mechanisms make harness optimization challenging. We first introduce VideoHarness-BRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework that evolves video harnesses around a frozen vision-language model. Analyzing over 4,000 evolved candidates, we find it competitive with hand-engineered systems but identify three interconnected failure modes: validation overfitting, search-budget dilution, and the early-experience trap. We trace all three to a common root: the same imperfect validation evidence drives both harness revisions and the proposer's search strategy. We therefore propose VideoHarness-SRSI, an evidence-governed framework in which every search decision rests on evidence that is transferable, sufficient, and gathered before the search commits. It restricts the proposer to content-free feedback, informs exploration with instrumented warm-up experiments, and develops mechanisms in isolated probe-race branches before factorial composition and joint refinement. Across four video understanding benchmarks, VideoHarness-SRSI improves the equally weighted mean held-out score by 6.2% relative to VideoHarness-BRSI and reduces the mean validation-test gap by 37.9%. Reliable harness evolution thus depends on how search is organized and informed, not only on how well it optimizes validation performance.

articles.title: Robust Real-Time Monocular Human Pose Estimation with Insole-Based Sensor Fusion
articles.excerpt: Real-time monocular human pose estimation is an important sensing component for human-centered intelligent systems. While recent camera-based methods have achieved impressive accuracy, fundamental challenges persist, particularly when visual observations are incomplete, such as during lower-body occlusion or short out-of-frame intervals. In these challenging but common scenarios, vision-only systems often struggle to reconstruct physically plausible lower-limb motion and reliable foot-ground contact. Due to the highly unobtrusive and wearable nature of smart insoles, this paper investigates whether simple plantar pressure and acceleration sensors can effectively resolve these visually induced limitations. To systematically investigate this, we first collect a synchronized multimodal dataset and then propose a part-decoupled temporal fusion framework. The proposed model fuses foot-sensing features into the lower-body branch to compensate for incomplete visual evidence, while a lightweight coordinator exchanges information between the upper- and lower-body temporal representations to maintain whole-body consistency. The framework is evaluated with three representative real-time visual backbones based on 2D keypoints, 3D landmarks, and SMPL-based human mesh recovery. We evaluate our framework on three representative real-time visual backbones. Quantitative experiments demonstrate that incorporating simple foot sensors consistently improves pose accuracy, motion smoothness, and gait-related measurements over vision-only baselines, with the most significant gains observed under occlusion and short visual-dropout conditions. Ultimately, our results demonstrate that unobtrusive foot sensing provides vital and complementary physical observability when camera observations are temporarily unavailable.

articles.title: Holi-Spatial 360: Generative Reconstruction from Sparse Panoramas for Spatial Rendering and Intelligence
articles.excerpt: Spatial intelligence requires scalable 3D environments that are both photorealistic and semantically grounded, yet existing indoor datasets are dominated by room-scale captures and costly LiDAR acquisition. Online real-estate platforms offer abundant panoramas of diverse multi-room homes, but sparse viewpoints and texture-poor regions make reconstruction severely under-constrained. We introduce Holi-Spatial 360, a generative reconstruction and data curation framework for converting these panoramas into annotated multi-room 3D environments. Because reconstruction quality bounds subsequent generation, our Correspondence-Guided Geometric Optimization converts feed-forward reconstruction priors into reliable cross-view constraints and builds a coherent 3D Gaussian Splatting representation as 3D spatial memory. Adapted single-image and video priors then restore appearance and complete continuous trajectories while preserving observed content. The reconstructed scenes support arbitrary RGB-D rendering and an automated curation pipeline that combines end-to-end 3D grounding with VLM-based verification. Holi360 contains over 1K multi-room 3DGS scenes, more than 100K instance annotations, and 2M spatial question-answer pairs. We also introduce the Holi360 benchmark to evaluate the spatial understanding of VLMs in real-world, multi-room indoor environments. Experiments demonstrate superior reconstruction and curation quality under sparse panoramic inputs, while fine-tuning VLMs on Holi360 substantially improves spatial reasoning capabilities.

articles.title: Spectral World Renderer: Unified 3D Hyperspectral Unmixing
articles.excerpt: Cameras and the foundation models built on them recognize what a 3D scene contains, but not what it is made of: surfaces of the same colour can be different materials. articles.excerpt: Temporal action detection in long untrimmed videos suffers from inaccurate localization and low-quality proposals, especially with sparse annotations and ambiguous boundaries. Hybrid combines complementary video features with different localization cues, while Rank-Calibration adjusts proposal ranking confidence to reflect localization reliability and candidate competition. HyrCap treats dense query-based predictions as an over-complete temporal event hypothesis space. We define a staged evaluation protocol to separately measure event localization, segment-level semantic understanding, and combined event understanding performance. Experiments on public benchmarks show that HyrCap achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple metrics and provides a finer-grained paradigm and evaluation protocol for query-based event segmentation and annotation.

articles.title: RDCompGS: Rate-Distortion Optimization for Compression of 3D Gaussian Splatting with Image Codecs
articles.excerpt: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables high-quality, real-time novel view synthesis but requires significant storage and transmission resources. Mapping Gaussian attributes to 2D representations enables efficient compression using mature image codecs. However, Gaussian representations that achieve comparable rendering quality are generally treated similarly during optimization, despite substantial differences in coding rate, leading to limited rate-distortion (R-D) performance after compression. To address this limitation, we propose RDCompGS, a 3DGS compression method that enables overall R-D optimization of Gaussian representations with respect to subsequent coding. A differentiable estimate of the coding rate is incorporated into the R-D optimization with rendering distortion. The rate constraint adjustment model further regulates the R-D trade-off across different compression conditions. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that RDCompGS achieves average Bj{\o}ntegaard Delta Rate reductions of 37.84% and 49.31% with H.265/HEVC and JPEG XL, respectively. The estimated rate also shows a strong correlation with the actual bit-rate under different compression conditions.

articles.title: Remember, Revisit, Revise: Scaffold Memory for Long-Horizon 3D Geometry
articles.excerpt: Geometry foundation models estimate camera poses and 3D scene structure from video sequences, but maintaining consistent reconstructions over long horizons remains challenging. Feed-forward models process long sequences as independent, fixed-length frame windows and align their predictions, causing pose and reconstruction errors to accumulate across windows. Streaming models retain information from past frames to inform future predictions, but cannot revise earlier estimates when later observations reveal errors. To address this, we introduce Scaffold MemOry for Revision (SMORE), a framework equipping frozen geometry foundation models with a revisable external memory for long-horizon inference. Inspired by hippocampal associative memory in biological brains, which links spatial context with sensory experience, SMORE associates where an observer is with what it observes, enabling past observations to be stored, retrieved, verified against new evidence, and revised when inconsistencies are detected. We evaluate SMORE with eight competitive geometry models on five datasets spanning camera pose estimation, multi-view depth estimation, 3D point-cloud reconstruction, simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), and novel view synthesis. Across all evaluated models, SMORE consistently improves long-sequence pose estimation, reduces multi-view depth error by up to 58%, reduces Chamfer distance for 3D point-cloud reconstruction by up to 43%, and achieves average trajectory error as low as 2.9 cm in long-horizon SLAM. By retaining corrected poses and observations, SMORE further improves the fidelity and spatial consistency of large-scale 3D scene reconstruction. These results establish revisable external memory as a flexible interface for extending pretrained geometry models beyond fixed-context prediction toward iterative, error-correcting inference over long visual sequences.

articles.title: MicroSDF: Microfacet-Driven Hybrid Neural SDFs for Mixed-Reflectance Surface Reconstruction
articles.excerpt: Accurate 3D reconstruction in real-world environments remains a significant challenge due to the coexistence of reflective and non-reflective surfaces, which pose distinct modeling demands. Existing methods often treat these surface types separately, limiting their generalizability and physical plausibility. To bridge this gap, we propose MicroSDF, a novel neural implicit framework that facilitates geometry and reflectance modeling through microfacet theory. Our approach incorporates three core innovations: (i) a microfacet-guided geometry model that extracts multi-scale surface normals (macroscopic and microfacet) from a signed distance field (SDF), regularized by a proposed microfacet normal consistency loss to enforce physically plausible surface orientations; (ii) an enhanced dual-branch color model, where the specular branch leverages the microfacet normals to model high-frequency reflectance, and the vanilla branch, unlike prior works, uses reflection direction (instead of viewing direction) to better model diffuse and low-frequency specular components; and (iii) a detection-guided color blending strategy that adaptively fuses the color outputs based on reflection priors, providing more physically intuitive blending than implicitly learned blending weights. Combined with a tailored multi-stage optimization scheme, the proposed MicroSDF achieves robust and high-fidelity reconstruction across reflective and non-reflective surfaces. Extensive experiments on DTU, Shiny Blender, Ref-NeRF, and DeepVoxels datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, establishing a new direction for physically grounded neural reconstruction.

articles.title: Mitigating Video Hallucinations via Attention-Guided Representation Perturbation
articles.excerpt: Video large language models (Video LLMs) often generate responses unsupported by the input video. Contrastive decoding (CD) can mitigate these hallucinations, but its effectiveness depends on how the negative branch weakens visual evidence. Existing methods rely on predefined perturbations or masking guided by question reconstruction, offering limited control over the model's visual reliance during answer generation. We introduce Attention-guided Representation Perturbation for Contrastive Decoding (ARP-CD), a training-free framework for constructing contrastive negatives directly in representation space. ARP-CD uses the attention mass assigned to visual tokens at the answer-prediction position to guide bounded gradient updates of the language model's input visual hidden states. These updates reduce visual attention and produce a negative input, whose predictions are contrasted with those of the original branch throughout generation. Experiments across four Video LLMs and four benchmarks show that ARP-CD outperforms representative training-free baselines in most model--benchmark settings, reducing hallucinations while improving general video understanding. Further analyses show that attention-guided perturbation directions improve negative quality and that the resulting negatives provide effective contrastive references for correcting the original predictions.

articles.title: A Diagnostic Study of World-Space Human Recovery Under High Camera Dynamics
articles.excerpt: Monocular world-space human recovery methods excel on current benchmarks, but these rarely include fast camera motion. We introduce the K-Pop stress test, broadcast dance videos that combine fast, large camera motion with dense multi-person choreography. Leading methods produce plausible per-frame meshes on these videos, yet their world-space trajectories drift far from the performers' stage positions. Through a systematic diagnosis, we show that the camera and human estimates each remain self-consistent, and that the drift appears when they are combined at mismatched scales. Each is recovered at its own scale, so a mismatch between the two can turn camera motion into human drift that grows with camera displacement and becomes severe in broadcast dance videos. We derive a closed-form correction that estimates this mismatch and applies one scale to all performers, removing the drift while keeping their relative positions in one shared world frame. It requires no retraining and works with existing backends. Combined with physical constraints, the correction yields stable world-space reconstruction for choreography modeling, scene editing, data generation, and virtual reshooting.

articles.title: FPV-CRASH: A Dataset for Offline Crash Moment Localization in Drone First-Person-View Videos
articles.excerpt: Crash Moment Localization aims to localize the major physical impact that interrupts controlled flight in an onboard first-person-view (FPV) video recorded by a drone, thereby providing a temporal reference for retrospective crash analysis in aerial robotics. However, existing crash-video datasets predominantly target surveillance or dash-camera footage, and their annotation schemes and task formulations are not designed for temporal localization of the major physical impact in UAV onboard FPV videos. To address this gap, we present FPV-CRASH, a dataset and fixed-protocol reference evaluation for offline Crash Moment Localization in drone FPV videos. FPV-CRASH contains 1,052 drone FPV clips (526 Crash and 526 Normal); each Crash clip has a single-frame reference annotation for the Crash Moment, and every clip is paired with four English captions automatically generated from sampled frames and the known Crash/Normal label. Normal clips carry no timestamp target and provide training-time background supervision. The captions support an auxiliary Text-to-Video Retrieval task, whereas localization inference remains video-only. We further provide a heatmap-based reference model that estimates a continuous Crash Moment timestamp from sparsely sampled frames. Under the fixed, non-source-disjoint clip-level protocol, the reference model reduces MAE from 1.12 s for the strongest fixed timing-prior baseline to 0.56 s (a 50% relative reduction) and achieves a median absolute error (MedAE) of 0.33 s; the fraction of clips localized within 0.5 s rises from 37.14% to 65.71%. The release includes annotations, available source video identifiers and URLs, clipping metadata, fixed split lists, and preprocessing code so that the reportable portion can be reconstructed without redistributing source footage. At submission time, all source-compilation URLs remained accessible.

articles.title: PhyMetric: Diagnosing Physical Plausibility in Text-to-Video Generation via Scene-Level QA
articles.excerpt: Text-to-video (T2V) generation models can produce visually realistic videos that nevertheless violate the physical consequences implied by the prompt and scene. Existing benchmarks largely rely on holistic plausibility scores or broad quality dimensions, leaving it unclear which physical behavior is being tested and why a model fails. We introduce PhyMetric, a scene-level diagnostic benchmark that recasts physical plausibility evaluation as verifiable, scene-grounded question answering. PhyMetric contains 1{,}115 scenes spanning 50 physical categories across six domains, paired with 8{,}920 answer-balanced binary questions over 12 evaluation dimensions. Each scene is associated with eight targeted yes/no questions and a structured physical prior specifying the governing law, expected temporal sequence, observable signatures, and common failure modes. At evaluation time, a vision-language model (VLM) judge answers each question from question-aware sampled frames conditioned on the prior, and correctness is hierarchically aggregated into scene, dimension, physical category, and model scores. Experiments on four open-source T2V models and three VLM judges show that scene-specific binary QA is a critical component of the protocol: when each targeted question is replaced by a single generic plausibility query, evaluator accuracy drops to the chance level. Structured physical priors offer a complementary signal that improves human alignment of the resulting scores, with effects that vary across VLM judges of different capacity. These findings establish PhyMetric as a benchmark that turns physical plausibility evaluation from opaque holistic scoring into interpretable, scene-level inspection. Our project page is available at: https://mengsiwei.github.io/PhyMetric/.

articles.title: DeltaStreamer: Towards Human-Like Agentic Streaming Video Understanding
articles.excerpt: We propose DeltaStreamer, a novel agentic framework for streaming video understanding inspired by how humans observe, remember, and investigate. Streaming video understanding requires a system to retain evidence before knowing which details future queries will need. Existing approaches often obscure event transitions and omit relevant details when compressing video history, and cannot recover missing visual evidence. DeltaStreamer addresses these limitations by combining change-aware memory with query-driven planning and targeted evidence gathering with replay. Before a query arrives, it continuously observes the stream and explicitly records visual changes in structured memory, preserving how events unfold rather than only what is present. When a query arrives, a query-driven planner identifies the required evidence and guides memory retrieval and targeted replay. By revisiting historical frames, the agent can recover visual details omitted during observation and ground its answer in evidence beyond the retained descriptions. This connects continuous observation with active investigation tailored to each question. Experiments on OVO-Bench and StreamingBench demonstrate improvements over representative streaming video understanding methods, with overall scores of 66.07% and 59.53%, respectively. Project page: https://bbbbchan.github.io/DeltaStreamer/

articles.title: OmniPoser: Flexible Human Motion Recovery in the Wild with Masked Flow Matching
articles.excerpt: Recovering 3D human motion from sparse wearable sensors is challenging due to the inherent noise, occlusion, and instability of real-world tracking signals. Existing approaches are restricted to fixed sensor configurations and, when built on diffusion models, are computationally prohibitive for real-time deployment. We propose OmniPoser, a universal framework that recovers full-body SMPL motion from a flexible combination of heterogeneous inputs, such as 3D keypoints, sparse IMU rotations, head-mounted 6-DoF poses, or any subset thereof, within a single model. OmniPoser introduces a cross-modal masking mechanism paired with a Masked Conditioning Encoder, enabling one architecture to incorporate diverse sensor configurations through a masked design. A decoupled dual-stream generative backbone generates complete motion via Conditional Flow Matching, requiring only a single ODE integration step at inference. articles.content: Recovering 3D human motion from sparse wearable sensors is challenging due to the inherent noise, occlusion, and instability of real-world tracking signals. Existing approaches are restricted to fixed sensor configurations and, when built on diffusion models, are computationally prohibitive for real-time deployment. We propose OmniPoser, a universal framework that recovers full-body SMPL motion from a flexible combination of heterogeneous inputs, such as 3D keypoints, sparse IMU rotations, head-mounted 6-DoF poses, or any subset thereof, within a single model. OmniPoser introduces a cross-modal masking mechanism paired with a Masked Conditioning Encoder, enabling one architecture to incorporate diverse sensor configurations through a masked design. A decoupled dual-stream generative backbone generates complete motion via Conditional Flow Matching, requiring only a single ODE integration step at inference. Across three settings and seven benchmarks, including in-the-wild Nymeria and Ego-Exo4D datasets, OmniPoser performs on par with state-of-the-art methods while running at over 700 FPS. The project page is available at https://jamesbridgewater51.github.io/omniposer-eccv/.

articles.title: CoDy: Codec Dynamics as Complementary Priors for Unsupervised Temporal Action Localization
articles.excerpt: Unsupervised temporal action localization (UTAL) aims to identify action categories and localize their temporal boundaries without annotation supervision. Existing methods typically derive supervision for both tasks solely from RGB and optical-flow representations, often resulting in noisy category assignments and inaccurate temporal boundaries. In this work, we reveal an overlooked property of video codecs: group-of-pictures quantization patterns preserve category-discriminative dynamics, while motion-vector and residual variations exhibit pronounced responses around action transitions. Based on this insight, we propose CoDy, a codec dynamics-guided framework that exploits the codec as complementary information to the visual view for UTAL. CoDy integrates a codec-enhanced view with RGB and flow through confidence-aware consensus clustering, producing reliable soft pseudo-labels. It further converts codec dynamics into a class-agnostic boundary prior, which supervises visual boundary learning and guides proposal initialization and iterative refinement. The codec branches are only used during the training stage and introduce no extra codec-side computation at inference. Extensive experiments on THUMOS14 and ActivityNet v1.3 demonstrate that CoDy consistently outperforms existing UTAL methods and achieves state-of-the-art localization performance. These results establish codec signals as effective annotation-free priors for jointly inferring which actions occur and when they occur.

articles.title: DreamHMR: From Video Generation to Human Motion Modeling via Structural Focusing
articles.excerpt: Human mesh recovery (HMR) provides a geometric foundation for understanding human motion, but accurately reconstructing both body motion and fine hand articulation from videos remains challenging, especially in real-world scenes where occlusion and partial visibility are common. Video generation pretraining offers rich spatial and temporal priors for this task, but its focus on visual synthesis leaves a gap between these representations and explicit human geometry. We present DreamHMR, a general framework that adapts video generation priors for complete body-and-hand reconstruction. It follows a global-to-local strategy, first grounding video representations in human geometry and then refining body and hand detail with reliable local evidence. Global Body Representation Transfer trains the video backbone to predict complete human renderings, turning its native prediction task into a means of learning surface correspondence and posed geometry. Local Joint Feature Enhancement combines contextual estimates with reliable local evidence to recover fine body and hand detail, while limiting interference from occluders and background. Experiments on five datasets with four video backbones demonstrate strong reconstruction performance across backbone families. Under a unified evaluation protocol, our best model outperforms the best existing methods on all reported metrics of 3DPW, EMDB-1, and RICH, reducing body MPJPE by 4.2%, 4.7%, and 6.1%, respectively. In more challenging occlusion settings on held-out BEDLAM and EgoBody sequences, DreamHMR reduces overall body and hand MPJPE by 7.0% and 10.0%, respectively. Our code will be made publicly available.

articles.title: These workers help train robots who could one day steal their jobs
articles.excerpt: Factory workers in India are being asked to wear GoPro cameras to record the way they do their jobs. The ultimate goal is to train robots to take over. Will it work?

articles.title: 新鸭绿江大桥延宕12年终通车 中国力图恢复对朝影响力
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/新鸭绿江大桥延宕12年终通车-中国力图恢复对朝影响力/a-79670658?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 延宕十余年的新鸭绿江大桥周四正式通车，连接中国丹东与朝鲜新义州。此次通车距朝俄公路桥开通约一个月。分析人士认为，大桥有望提振双边贸易，也反映北京希望恢复对朝鲜的独特影响力。

articles.title: 德语媒体：德国对华政策出现“时代转折”？
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：德国对华政策出现-时代转折-？/a-79670594?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 欧盟峰会召开之际，《法兰克福汇报》发表评论称，从欧盟对华政策的刹车片，到德法联手推动强硬威慑工具，德国的对华政策已经悄然出现“时代转折”。《商报》评论则认为，默茨新对华政策成功与否，也将决定德国的内政走向。

articles.title: 北溪爆炸案在德国开审 被告律师称北溪管道或为“合法打击目标”
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/北溪爆炸案在德国开审-被告律师称北溪管道或为-合法打击目标/a-79670573?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 被控主导北溪天然气管道爆炸案的乌克兰前军官，目前正在德国受审。庭审期间，其辩护律师辩称，北溪管道属于“侵略方的基础设施”，因此可能是合法的军事打击目标。

articles.title: 欧盟召开峰会：对华出口、能源价格及预算是重点
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/欧盟召开峰会：对华出口、能源价格及预算是重点/a-79669593?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 本周四（10月15日），欧盟领导人在布鲁塞尔开启为期两天的峰会，讨论如何遏制中国出口激增、应对高昂的能源价格，并弥合各方在欧盟未来预算问题上的巨大分歧。对乌克兰的支持、安全与防务、移民、欧盟扩容以及中东局势也是讨论的议题。

articles.title: 习近平“5年10万”之邀：是搭桥还是挖坑？
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/习近平-5年10万-之邀：是搭桥还是挖坑？/a-79668378?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 习近平访美期间宣布，邀请10万名美国青年在五年内赴华交流学习。支持者认为，美国急需培养新一代中国通；批评者则担心学生遭到灌输、监控，甚至在危机中沦为"人质"。

articles.title: 黄奇帆落马 为什么有人惋惜？
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/黄奇帆落马-为什么有人惋惜？/a-79662742?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 重庆前市长黄奇帆在卸任后多年被官宣落马，引起广泛关注，也令不少人感到惋惜。他不仅是经历重庆官场多次震荡而安然无恙的昔日“不倒翁”，还被誉为既有专业素养又敢说真话的”网红经济学家“。

articles.title: 德语媒体：学术自由不能跨越国家安全的底线
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：学术自由不能跨越国家安全的底线/a-79662535?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 《商报》客座评论指出，科研自由不能成为忽视安全风险的理由，德国政府应加强科研领域的安全保障，为德中科研合作明确界限。《新苏黎世报》评论认为，本年度诺贝尔和平奖授予前联合国人权事务高级专员皮莱的决定值得商榷，因为正是在她任内，联合国人权机构沦落成了专制国家的工具。

articles.title: 德国为何转向支持欧盟对华贸易强硬？
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德国为何转向支持欧盟对华贸易强硬？/a-79660045?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 在很长一段时间里，德国不愿对中国采取更为强硬的行动，担忧引发中方报复。多年来，柏林方面一直阻挠欧盟采取更强硬的立场来应对欧盟眼中的中国不公平贸易行为。然而随着关键行业面临的压力日益增大，德国政府也开始与法国一道，寻求赋予欧盟更强大的贸易防御权，以保护其工业基础。

articles.title: 中国出口暴增消费疲软 经济隐忧难化解
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/中国出口暴增消费疲软-经济隐忧难化解/a-79659242?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 官方最新数据显示，中国9月份进出口表现远超市场预期，前三季度贸易顺差逼近1万亿美元大关，有望刷新历史纪录。然而，在以半导体和汽车为代表的出口高歌猛进背后，国内消费却持续萎靡，北京依靠外需拉动增长的模式正引发美欧等主要贸易伙伴的强烈反弹。这种内外失衡的增长路径究竟还能持续多久？

articles.title: 台北市長爭奪戰的兩位主角：蔣萬安與沈伯洋是誰？
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/台北市長爭奪戰的兩位主角：蔣萬安與沈伯洋是誰？/a-79657998?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 台灣地方選舉將於11月底舉行，台北市長選舉受到高度關注。DW整理兩名主要候選人——國民黨籍現任市長蔣萬安、民進黨候選人沈伯洋——的重要生平與政治簡歷，以及他們過往對兩岸等議題的看法。

articles.title: 一場意外激烈的台北市長選舉：沈伯洋「洋流」可能逆轉勝蔣萬安嗎？
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/一場意外激烈的台北市長選舉：沈伯洋「洋流」可能逆轉勝蔣萬安嗎？/a-79647028?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 台灣2026年地方選戰進入倒數階段，台北市長選情似乎出現變化。原先不被看好的民進黨候選人沈伯洋聲勢大漲，被形容是「洋流」崛起，令現任市長、國民黨籍的蔣萬安尋求連任增添變數。「藍大於綠」的台北有可能翻盤嗎？DW採訪學者分析勝負關鍵。

articles.title: “蟑螂运动”再起 印度青年为什么抗议？
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/蟑螂运动-再起-印度青年为什么抗议？/a-79653322?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 今年5月，印度首席大法官把找不到工作的年轻人称作“蟑螂”，激起印度Z世代怒火，并促使他们成立“蟑螂人民党”（CJP）。如今时隔近半年，“蟑螂运动”再度风起云涌，显示印度年轻人对政府的不满加深。

articles.title: 争夺欧洲消费者 巴黎车展成中欧车企角力场
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/争夺欧洲消费者-巴黎车展成中欧车企角力场/a-79652085?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 今年巴黎车展开幕之际，正值欧盟与中国就混动车达成初步安排。欧洲汽车业凭借一系列新车型和欧盟的支持，试图在与中国车商争夺欧洲市场的竞争中重振旗鼓。

articles.title: 德语媒体：强硬立场已经初见成效
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：强硬立场已经初见成效/a-79652052?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 德媒《编辑部网络》评论写道，混动车协议避免了欧中之间一场迫在眉睫的贸易冲突，同时也证明，欧盟只有显示强硬的立场，才能换来北京的让步。《日报》评论认为，混动车领域的协议并不能缓解欧中贸易的严重失衡，对中国产品全面征收反补贴关税可能是欧盟的唯一选项。

articles.title: 重庆政坛“不倒翁”黄奇帆落马 卸任近十年后接受中纪委审查
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/重庆政坛-不倒翁-黄奇帆落马-卸任近十年后接受中纪委审查/a-79651497?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 重庆市原市长黄奇帆周二被宣布涉嫌严重违纪违法，正接受中央纪委国家监委纪律审查和监察调查。现年74岁的黄奇帆在重庆任职约15年，先后与六任市委书记共事，曾历经薄熙来、孙政才两任书记落马的官场震荡仍屹立不倒，近年以网红经济学家的身份到中国各地发表演讲。

articles.title: IMF最新增长预期：下调中国至4.5%，上调台湾至10.7%
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/imf最新增长预期：下调中国至4-5-，上调台湾至10-7/a-79649497?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 国际货币基金组织发布最新《世界经济展望》，将今年全球增长预期微升至3.1%。中国今年增长预期被下调至4.5%，德国被上调至1.3%。印度再次被预测为全球增长最快的主要经济体，今年增速预计为7.0%。台湾则被上调至惊人的10.7%。

articles.title: 德语媒体：“欧盟只是得到了一次喘息机会”
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：-欧盟只是得到了一次喘息机会/a-79643059?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 就上周举行的中欧贸易谈判，《商报》发表评论称，当前达成的妥协，并没有解决贸易失衡的根源。提高竞争力，减少对华依赖，才是欧盟的当务之急。《南德意志报》评论则认为，欧中谈判此次能够达成协议，说明欧盟对话与施压并举的双重战略已经开始奏效。

articles.title: 皮莱诺奖引发争议 被指控“维吾尔种族灭绝的共犯”
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/皮莱诺奖引发争议-被指控-维吾尔种族灭绝的共犯/a-79641904?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 2026年诺贝尔和平奖得主皮莱，曾在2010年担任联合国人权高专时谢绝出席刘晓波诺奖颁奖礼，被认为是“整体上令人钦佩的履历中的一个污点”。更严厉的批评来自人权律师埃玛·赖利（Emma Reilly），她指控皮莱“是维吾尔种族灭绝的共犯”。

articles.title: 还原说中文的“骗子警察”作案过程
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/还原说中文的-骗子警察-作案过程/a-79641355?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 说中文的骚扰电话并不少见，幸亏真正上钩的人并不多。《波恩汇报》近日报道了一名中国年轻女性被诈骗5万多欧的事件。

articles.title: 德国议会“中国委员会”建议欧盟须准备更强硬的对华贸易政策工具
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德国议会-中国委员会-建议欧盟须准备更强硬的对华贸易政策工具/a-79633330?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 德国联邦议院委托成立的专家委员会建议，欧盟必须在欧洲层面准备更强有力的贸易政策工具，以便在中国于贸易争端中采取升级措施时有能力实施反制。该委员会在首份半年度报告中指出，德国对华经济安全状况总体趋于恶化，供应链依赖加深，并认为“合作伙伴、竞争对手和制度性对手”的对华战略已告失败。

articles.title: 墙外文摘：张婉莹只监控了赖清德儿子吗？
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/墙外文摘：张婉莹只监控了赖清德儿子吗？/a-79632316?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 一个加州房产经纪人监控赖清德儿子做什么？有评论指出，房地产经纪人是最被要求保密与忠诚的职业之一，一旦违反这种职业特性，恰恰契合"特务"所需。

articles.title: 孟加拉与俄罗斯合建核电站年底启用 当地民众亦喜亦忧
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/孟加拉与俄罗斯合建核电站年底启用-当地民众亦喜亦忧/a-79581772?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 孟加拉首座核电站在经过长期拖延后，一号反应堆将于年底启用。该项目于2017年与俄罗斯合作开工建设，核电站所在地路布尔村已有了数千名俄罗斯人居住的社区。当地民众则喜忧参半。

articles.title: AI变SI：特朗普执意更名为哪般？
articles.excerpt: 美国总统特朗普威胁，凡不使用SI（超级智能），而继续使用AI（人工智能）的，将被白宫视为敌人。但专家说，更名“超级智能”并不能缓解公众对人工智能的忧虑。

articles.title: 长平观察：脖子上的铁链，嘴上的封条
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/长平观察：脖子上的铁链，嘴上的封条/a-79627398?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 北京女子孙美华失联26年后在山东被寻回，没有立案通报，却有一连串账号被封。时事评论作家长平指出，这起最新的“铁链女”事件更进一步揭示了中国政府在人口拐卖中扮演的角色。

articles.title: 英国女学生发起请愿：呼吁禁止色情片中使用校服元素
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/英国女学生发起请愿：呼吁禁止色情片中使用校服元素/a-79627348?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 短裙、过膝袜、白衬衫：校服一直是色情影片中十分泛滥的装扮元素。如今，几名英国女学生决定打破这一现状——她们发起了一项联名请愿。

articles.title: 特朗普再次逆转对俄制裁 宣布与普京达成柴油协议
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/特朗普再次逆转对俄制裁-宣布与普京达成柴油协议/a-79626933?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 就在上月刚刚签署一项以已故参议员格雷厄姆的名字命名对俄罗斯的新制裁法案之后，特朗普周五宣布同意俄罗斯向美国和全球市场供应俄罗斯柴油。分析人士认为，面对中期选举压力，特朗普总是选择对自己个人有利的做法，而非国会已经作出的决定。

articles.title: 德语媒体：财政吃紧 北京盯上了富豪们的境外资产
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：财政吃紧-北京盯上了富豪们的境外资产/a-79618435?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 《新苏黎世报》称，经济疲软和房地产危机使中国财政收入急剧下滑，各地方政府目前都在想法设法扩展财路，富豪们的海外投资收益也成了税务追缴的重点。《经济周刊》评论称，德法联手建议欧盟采取强硬对华政策，标志着柏林已经不愿继续听从北京的摆布。

articles.title: 德语媒体：向北京亮剑， 欧盟有足够底气吗？
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：向北京亮剑，-欧盟有足够底气吗？/a-79599152?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 《法兰克福汇报》评论称，欧盟拟议中的强硬反制措施，或许能给正在北京进行的欧中谈判增添筹码，但威慑未必能使北京做出让步，欧洲增强自身实力才是硬道理。《南德意志报》评论也认为，强硬政策并不能保障欧盟在对华竞争中立于不败之地。

articles.title: 德语媒体：“不能因惧怕死亡而选择自杀”
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：-不能因惧怕死亡而选择自杀/a-79582805?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 《商报》评论称，欧盟在对华贸易政策上采取强硬路线，可能会招致北京的报复，但因害怕报复就不去作为，就等同于“因惧怕死亡而选择经济上的自杀”。《日报》评论称，德法两国扩大欧盟反制权限的建议，终于让欧盟拥有了“快速反击”的可能性。

articles.title: 欧洲AI出大招 法国Mistral推出超强模型
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/欧洲ai出大招-法国mistral推出超强模型/a-79582475?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 法国AI新创公司Mistral被称为“欧洲的OpenAI”。这家公司在创造型人工智能产品方面的每个更新都备受关注，被看好能让欧洲在AI领域摆脱对美国和中国竞争对手的依赖甚至威胁。
